sentences.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to the slow English podcast. I am Emily, your host. Today,
we are traveling to a beautiful city in Africa called Acra. Acra is the capital city of Ghana.
It is on the coast of the Atlantic Ocean. Acra is a lively city with colorful markets,
busy streets, and friendly people. Part two, where is Acra? Acra is in West Africa.
It is on the southern coast of Ghana. The city is near the ocean and has many beaches. Acra is also
close to the countryside and hills. It is a very busy city but also has calm places to relax.
Part three, a short history. Acra is a city with a long history. People have lived here for hundreds of
years. In the past, there were forts and trading posts. Acra grew as a trade city with gold, cocoa,
and other products. Ghana became independent in 1957 and Acra became the capital.
Today, Acra is modern and still has old historical sites. Part four, what does Acra look like?
Acra has many modern buildings, streets, and shopping centers. It also has old neighborhoods
with small houses and traditional markets. The city has green parks and wide roads. You can see
the Atlantic Ocean in some parts of the city. Acra is colorful and full of life. Part five,
famous places to visit. There are many interesting places in Acra. Independent Square, a big square
for celebrations, Kwame Nakruma Mausoleum, a monument for Ghana's first president,
Makola Market, a busy market with food, clothes, and crafts, Jamestown, an old part of the city
with lighthouses and history, La Body Beach, a famous beach to relax and enjoy the sun.
Part six, food and Acra. Ghanaian food is delicious and spicy. People eat a lot of rice,
beans, plantains, and fish. A popular dish is Banco and Tilapia. Another favorite food is
jalaf rice, rice with tomato sauce and spices. Street food is very common in Acra. You can eat
fried plantain, kebabs, and acara on the streets. Part seven, the people of Acra. People in Acra
are friendly and talkative. Most people speak English because it is the official language.
Many people also speak Tuis, Ga, and other local languages. Families are very important in Ghana.
People enjoy meeting friends, dancing, and listening to music.
Part eight, music and culture. Acra is full of music and culture. Ghana is famous for
high life and hip life music. Many people dance to music in the streets, festivals, and clubs.
The city has art centers, theaters, and cultural events. Traditional dances and colorful clothes
are part of daily life. Part nine, nature and Acra. Acra is close to beautiful nature.
The beaches are perfect for walking and swimming. There are parks like legon botanical gardens.
People enjoy nature walks, picnics, and bird watching. In the city, you can also see palm trees
and gardens. Part 10, daily life in Acra. Life in Acra is busy but friendly. People go to work,
school, or markets. Transportation includes buses, taxis, and trotros shared many buses.
In the evenings, families relax at home or visit friends. Weekends are for shopping,
music, and festivals. People in Acra love to spend time together.
Part 11, learning English in Acra. English is the main language in Acra. Schools teach English
from a young age. You can easily speak English with locals. Visiting Acra is a good way to
learn some local words in Twi or Ga. People are happy when tourists try to speak their language.
Part 12, goodbye from Acra. Our journey in Acra is now finished. We learned about the city's history,
markets, beaches, food, and people. Acra is a city full of colors, life, and culture.
to the Slow English Podcast. I am Emily and I hope you can visit Acra one day. Goodbye or as
Canadians sometimes say, bye bye.
